caption: The drawing consists of three views of a single metallic object, depicted in grayscale pencil on a plain, off-white background. The object appears to be a three-dimensional device with irregular, looping, and curved forms, resembling a set of connected loops or clamps, with three flat-topped cylindrical pegs for support. The main part of the object has two large rounded openings connected by a narrow section, with an extended straight handle-like feature terminating in a tightly coiled loop at one end. The top left view is a plan (top-down) representation of the object, showing the outline and the position of the pegs. Directly below it is a side view, showing the height of the pegs and the flat lower edge of the device. The lower part of the paper features a larger, three-quarters perspective drawing, offering a sense of depth and dimension; from this angle, the thickness and texture of the material are visible, as well as the height and placement of the pegs. A short scale is drawn beneath the side view in the upper portion, indicating the object's size. The lower right corner contains a small signature: "J. Lipkin."
title: Flat Iron Holder
